b: Nice post. I'm one of the few people around who's used all four plus an Oticon Connect Clip. For me, LE Audio wins by quite a long way.

I have the Oticon Intent but just got the Oticon Easy LE Adapter. It only works with Oticon HA but is a small USB-C dongle. I’ve used it on my iPhone 16 Pro, iPad, and work PC. Basically you pair your hearing aids to the dongle and plug it into the USBC port on the device you want Bluetooth LE Audio and then it works. I can stream and take calls on my PC by plugging the device into the USB C port. Same with my iPad or iPhone (which can pair using the app but the dongle is a much stronger and stable connection. Works like the TV3 device. I got it from my Audiologist last week and just started playing with it. So far it’s fantastic and add LE Audio to any device. It says that it’s not for Apple devices but it works just fine and I tried it on three different devices. Good luck but this is the way!

All good points. It is brand locked to Oticon and only works with Intent and maybe Zeal. I’ve been testing it out in various scenarios. I’ve been able to turn off Bluetooth on my phone, plug in the adapter and get calls and streaming media to my hearing aids. For me this is a game change to be able to use on my work computer since I have a lot of Zoom and Teams meetings. I told my audiologist I’d report back in a month. So far I’m the first patient to ask about and they let me have the one unit in the office to try.

I was pretty surprised but I think I’m more tech savvy and interested than most of her patients. I moved from the Oticon More w to the Intent 1 because 1. My hearing needed it and 2. I needed a better more stable Bluetooth connection. The Intent are better at keeping both HA’s connected but I still experience drop offs. I’ve been researching anything I can find to make the Bluetooth better and more stable. I came across the Easy LE Adapter in my research. I think it’s a pretty new device and unless the Oticon Reps talk about it you won’t know that it even exists.  My audiologist thought it only helped to get AuraCast but it does so much more. 

I’ll report back.

I dig my heels in when I see a device is locked to a brand. I've got an Avantree dongle that does the same thing as far as I know. A big selling point of LE Audio for me is that it should make devices interoperable.

The Easy LE Adapter does work on your Philips 9050, too!

What I like about it is it's low profile, unlike the CR82 Aura.

Also, is the connection significantly more stable when using the adapter? For example, would I be able to keep my phone in my pants pocket without the connection cutting out, whereas it sometimes does with the direct Bluetooth connection?

If I left Bluetooth on my iPhone turned on and have the adapter plugged in it also works fine. The HA seem to be paired to the phone through either Bluetooth or the LE Adapter but everything stays paired. I tested leaving the adapter in but turning off Bluetooth and it works. If I unplug the adapter with Bluetooth off then I lose connection. If I keep Bluetooth on and take out the adapter it still stays connected. 

I’m happy to play around and try anything else that you can think of. I did the same thing in an iPad Pro and an iPad Mini 7. I’ll try to see if the adapter works in an Android device this week and try a Mac Air and PC. I’ll share whatever I find out.

I actually tried the Easy LE Adapter with Signia Hearing Aids and it worked aswell.

The Connect Clip. You had to wear it around your neck. Easy to lose (I lost two). Latenchy from the BT classic audio. Just fiddly.

mfi and ASHA. Definitely better than nothing. Occasional glitching and connection issues. Sound quality is adequate. Range is just ok.

Bluetooth classic audio (trial of Phonak Audeo 90). Better audio quality than mfi and ASHA. Short dropouts every 20 minutes or so. Other people report better or worse experiences than this.

LE Audio. Once connected, it's connected. No glitching, no dropouts. Experience has gradually improved with updates to phone and hearing aids. I spent some time switching between LE Audio and ASHA on my phone and comparing the sound. Subjectively for me, LE Audio is a more natural sound. ASHA is 'flatter'. Best description I can come up with at short notice. I got the best range out of LE Audio. Slightly better than 'classic'. Outdoors I

Dates the three of us then. Something that looks and sounds like an airpod, uses LE Audio and can act as a hearing aid- including for severe losses- for short periods of time... that's what I want.

Another very important factor is the Acoustics! The balanced armature drivers in HAs are not capable of frequencies below 80 to 100 Hz, and  (Oticon Intents can drop to 80, most can't). Upper end is maxed out at 10KHz, which most HA users can't hear anyway.

You need occluded earmolds to really take advantage of streaming audio, as well, so that's another factor. Most audis' don't consider earmolds, and fit patients with open domes, which leaks out whatever low frequencies there are. Once again, acoustics.

If they ever move into MEMS, we may have some ability to challenge good IEMs or Pods.

LEA is as good as it gets, for now, and with a phone that suports it, coupled with LEA HAs you can get decent streaming audio, but it ain't HiFi!

>Your aids "taking over" all audio on Android is by design. Under ASHA and LE Audio, Android registers hearing aids as an accessibility device and gives them priority for media routing.
